title: Direct OpenCode HTTP Design Lifecycle Smoke Result
claim: The MCP bridge successfully used the direct OpenCode HTTP lifecycle path for a bounded design-only model interaction, without contacting the remote runner start endpoint, starting OpenCode, calling wait, or leaving the created session behind.
summary: FP-MCP-288 records that the direct OpenCode HTTP path is operational beyond read-only status checks. A minimal assistant-completion probe succeeded, and a bounded pure-design lifecycle prompt for MCP server.ts decomposition also succeeded after the first operation-worded prompt was correctly blocked by the lifecycle boundary. The successful lifecycle created one session, submitted one async prompt, observed the expected assistant marker SERVER_TS_REFACTOR_PLAN_READY, and deleted the session. This is sufficient to proceed toward a model-assisted server.ts refactor packet, while preserving the runner as legacy optional infrastructure.
caveats: The first design prompt was blocked by PROMPT_BLOCKED_BY_CANARY_BOUNDARY because it contained operation-like language; this is expected fail-closed behavior.
The successful design lifecycle returned only a bounded assistant excerpt in the tool result; full design content was not retained after cleanup.
No source code was modified by this checkpoint.
This does not yet prove a model can safely perform code edits through the direct HTTP path; it proves bounded design interaction works.
boundaries: OpenCode process not started by the MCP bridge

structuredRecord.nextWork: create a bounded model-assisted server.ts refactor implementation packet with explicit extraction scope and verification commands
